items.title: docs(design): refusal-triggered failover lane sketch (#14234)
items.body: Before: #3150's acceptance criterion 3, the design for what a request does after the seated models refuse it on content-policy grounds, had no artifact. Its triage notes also described the router as having no content-policy class at all. After: `doc/2026-11-25T01-55-00Z_design_refusal-failover-lane-14234/` records the sketch, and it is grounded in what the fork does today. The fork already classifies refusals as `ContentPolicy`, keeps them out of route health (#1084), and fails a refused request over within its pool. The only gap is what happens when every seated candidate refuses. The sketch covers four things: - **Trigger:** the existing `ContentPolicy` class, used only when the refusals are unanimous across at least two provider families. - **Failover:** a dedicated route head that only the policy-exhaustion branch can reach. It is tried once per request, needs no output started, keeps state intact, enforces a tool-capability floor, and is off by default. - **Telemetry:** a `trigger` field and a `failover_from` field, health isolation in both directions, and no body capture. - **Bounds:** lawful use only, privacy terms, an outbound credential gate, a benchmark plan for Abliteration large-flash and Venice Uncensored 1.2, and a named pilot-approval gate. How: a design document only. No code, config, seating, accounts or purchases. Fixes #14234 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id/web): bound format_unix_timestamp — closed-form, reject out-of-range (#934)
items.body: Fixes #934. Queue task 1084 (repo-health-code-pilot). ## Problem `format_unix_timestamp` looped year-by-year from 1970 with no range check. Timestamps come from unvalidated tag names/metadata, so one huge value (e.g. a file named `x.archive.18446744073709551615`, or `modified = u64::MAX`) hung every file-list render, persistently. ## Fix - Reject out-of-range timestamps up front: anything past `9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC` (the last 4-digit-year instant) returns an empty string — the file list already renders empty as "no date". - Replace the year loop with the closed-form civil-from-days algorithm (Howard Hinnant): constant time for every accepted input, byte-identical output for all in-range values (verified against a reference implementation over 2000+ sampled timestamps plus every test expectation). ## Tests New `web::templates` unit tests: - normal values unchanged (epoch, 2000-02-29 leap day, 2024-10-01) - `u64::MAX` → empty (previously ~5.8e11 loop iterations) - millisecond-scale value → empty - year-9999 boundary: `253402300799` → `9999-12-31 23:59`; `+1` → empty Verification runs on CI per the task packet: `cargo test --features web --lib web::templates`. --- Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): make the log_sync batch-collection tests deterministic (#3199)
items.body: Closes #3199. ## Problem The `log_sync` batch-collection tests paced arrivals every 2 ms from a second thread against the production idle grace of 5 ms (`BATCH_GRACE`). Any scheduler delay over 5 ms — routine on the loaded build machine — split the batch or ended it early. The `pkgs/id` check phase gates every NixOS system build, so this was a load-dependent coin flip on every deploy: it failed two switch attempts on 2026-10-31 at load 70–156 (`log_sync::tests::test_batch_collection_refused_stream_ends_at_the_total_cap`, suite 1986 passed / 1 failed). ## Fix The grace is now a parameter of `collect_batch`: - The production caller (`ingest_arrivals`) passes `BATCH_GRACE` — production behaviour and tuning are byte-for-byte unchanged. - The pacing-sensitive tests inject `TEST_GRACE` (250 ms — 50x production), beyond any plausible pacing hiccup, while the pacing itself stays at the production-like 2 ms. - The grace-restart test now paces 200 arrivals (~400 ms) so the run still spans far longer than the injected grace: it keeps proving the grace is an idle wait that restarts per arrival, not a total window. - The refused-stream cap test asserts "ended while the stream was still flowing" by checking the pacer directly (it cannot have finished when the batch returns at the cap) instead of comparing wall-clock elapsed against the nominal pace, which raced the pacer's own scheduling. No test deleted, skipped, or `#[ignore]`d; no assertion weakened — the cap test still proves a refused stream ends the batch at `BATCH_MAX_ARRIVALS` mid-stream. The one other pacing user, `test_ingest_tallies_refusals_and_commits_queued_headers`, asserts only the final tally, which batch boundaries cannot change; audited and left unchanged. ## Verification (laptop, this tree) - Batch family (`test_batch_collection`, 5 tests): passed in all 10 `log_sync`-module runs and 5/5 dedicated runs, at 5-minute loads from ~58 to ~105 — the conditions that used to split batches at a 5 ms margin no longer matter at a 250 ms injected grace. - Full `log_sync` module (19 tests): 3/3 consecutive clean runs after the incident below, plus 5 clean runs interleaved earlier. - Full check suite: `nix build .#id-web` on this tree — see the #3199 comment for the result line. ## Incident note (not this change) Mid-verification the laptop root disk hit 100% (3.2T/3.2T, 0 available), which made unrelated `log_sync` *session* tests fail progressively (store writes failing) and broke git. A `nix-collect-garbage` pass freed 1.2T (325k store paths); the session tests returned to 19/19 immediately after, on the same binary. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Expanded coverage for paced arrivals and refusal-only streams, including behavior at the total-arrival cap while the producer is still running.
